answers.explanation: 256 − 224 = 32. Subnets start at .0, .32, .64, .96, and so on.
Block size 64. 77 is in the block that starts at 64.
The usable range is .65 to .126. Only .64 (network) and .127 (broadcast) are off limits.
8 subnets need 3 borrowed bits: 24 + 3 = /27, with 30 usable hosts each.
Block size 4 in the 3rd octet: 216 to 219. The broadcast is the last address, 10.104.219.255.
A /30 has 4 addresses: network, two hosts, broadcast. Nothing wasted.
Each subnet loses two addresses to its own network and broadcast, so you end up with slightly fewer. You subnet for structure and control, not for more addresses.
